item.text:
**4B.6 Research Note**

I found no credible 2024 evidence that Putin protected independent media or widened information access in any substantive sense. The record instead shows censorship, forced disclosure, blocking of foreign and domestic outlets, harassment of journalists, and expansion of surveillance over online speech.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Against | [Russia: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says the government controls most national television, radio, and print; laws on extremism, foreign agents, and undesirable organizations are used to harass media; Roskomnadzor blocks sites at the Justice Ministry’s request; and authorities have forced more than 300 media outlets to suspend operations since the 2022 invasion. | `4B.6`, `4B.3`, `4B.5` |
| Against | [Russia: Nations in Transit 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024 | Freedom House says the state propaganda apparatus expanded with fake news pages and fraudulent social accounts, 74 media outlets were labeled undesirable by October, independent journalists were prosecuted and assaulted, and foreign journalists such as Gershkovich and Kurmasheva remained imprisoned. | `4B.6`, `4B.3`, `4B.5` |
| Against | [Russia: Freedom on the Net 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-net/2024 | Freedom House reports a March 2024 ban on information about bypassing blocks and VPN advertising, expanded blocking powers, surveillance of online critics, and laws requiring platforms to remove content or hand over user data. This is censorship and access restriction, not protection of information freedom. | `4B.6`, `4B.3`, `4B.5` |
| Against | [Russia bans Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty as “undesirable”](https://cpj.org/2024/02/russia-bans-radio-free-europe-radio-liberty-as-undesirable/) | Committee to Protect Journalists | 2024-02-21 | https://cpj.org/2024/02/russia-bans-radio-free-europe-radio-liberty-as-undesirable/ | CPJ reports that Russian authorities added RFE/RL to the “undesirable” register, obstructing a major independent broadcaster and treating journalism itself as a hostile activity. | `4B.6`, `4B.3` |
| Against | [Russia to block leading foreign media outlets in retaliation against EU](https://cpj.org/2024/06/russia-to-block-leading-foreign-media-outlets-in-retaliation-against-eu/) | Committee to Protect Journalists | 2024-06-26 | https://cpj.org/2024/06/russia-to-block-leading-foreign-media-outlets-in-retaliation-against-eu/ | Russia blocked access to 81 European media outlets, including AFP, Der Spiegel, Le Monde, and public broadcasters, in retaliation for EU restrictions. That is a direct reduction in information access. | `4B.6`, `4B.3` |
| Against | [Law governing the provision of communications services to foreign nationals and specifying modalities for spreading information on social media](https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/news/74828) | President of Russia | 2024-08-08 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/news/74828 | Putin signed a law requiring social-media owners to provide user information to Roskomnadzor or the FSB on request and to label pages with over 10,000 users as registered. The same law adds biometric and SIM restrictions for foreign nationals. This is broad state control over information distribution and user identity, not media protection. | `4B.6`, `4B.5`, `4B.3` |
| Against | [Putin lets 'economically significant' entities limit information disclosures](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-01-29 | https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001 | Reuters reported that Putin widened secrecy privileges so entities deemed economically significant could stop disclosing information publicly. That reduces transparency and makes scrutiny of powerful actors harder. | `4B.6`, `4B.4` |

**Assessment**

- I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Putin protected independent media or information access.
- The best-documented pattern is the opposite: direct censorship, site blocking, forced registration, user-data access for security services, and punitive treatment of journalists and outlets.
- The only arguable “counter” is that Russia framed some actions as retaliation for EU media bans, but that is still a restriction on access, not protection of press freedom.

**Search gap**

- I did not find any credible 2024 source showing Putin took a real pro-media-freedom step, relaxed censorship, or reduced pressure on owners and journalists. The available evidence is consistently negative.
